Stop struggling to communicate in Japan. Kotomaji is the complete offline travel phrasebook with native audio pronunciation, 1,097 JLPT kanji, daily travel tips, and a built-in currency converter — everything you need to speak Japanese with confidence. Pay once, own it forever. No subscription.

MASTER 305+ REAL TRAVEL PHRASES

305 carefully selected phrases for real situations you'll encounter in Japan:

- Greetings and Japanese etiquette
- Restaurants and food
- Transportation (train, taxi, subway)
- Hotels and accommodations
- Shopping and bargaining
- Directions and navigation
- Medical emergencies
- Numbers and prices
- Culture and respect
- Useful everyday phrases

FREE: 204 essential phrases included
PRO: 101 additional premium phrases

OUTSTANDING FEATURES

REAL AND NATURAL AUDIO
- Over 570 professional audio recordings
- Male and female native speaker voices
- Normal and slow speed for practice
- Clear, natural pronunciation you can trust

LEARN KANJI, HIRAGANA & KATAKANA
- All 1,097 JLPT kanji (N5 to N1), plus hiragana and katakana in one place
- Level-by-level paths, from the first vowels to the trickiest kanji

- A final exam for every level, with a special seal for a perfect score

INTEGRATED CURRENCY CONVERTER

- No additional app needed

DAILY JAPAN TRAVEL TIPS
- Etiquette, transport, and money-saving advice

ALL-NEW DESIGN (VERSION 5.0)
- Complete visual redesign

- Smooth animations and micro-interactions

INTERACTIVE PHRASES WITH NUMBERS

PREMIUM USER EXPERIENCE

show_hn.title: Show HN: Built and shipped an iOS app from my phone while traveling Japan

quotes.text:
I wanted to see how far I could push remote development.

Before leaving for Japan, I configured my Mac at home to never sleep, set up VPN + SSH access, and used persistent terminal sessions so I could keep everything running remotely.

During the trip, I built and shipped a native iOS app entirely from my phone.

No laptop.
No local Xcode.
All builds triggered remotely and deployed to TestFlight.

The app itself is a lightweight Japanese travel phrase app we actually used during the trip. Fully offline. We pre-generated TTS audio and bundled it so it worked in stations, underground areas, and rural zones without connectivity.

What made it interesting wasn’t the app itself, but the feedback loop.

We would test phrases in real restaurants and train stations during the day, notice friction, tweak things that evening over SSH from a hotel or ryokan, ship a new build, and use the improved version the next morning.

It felt less like building in a simulated environment and more like building inside the exact context the product was meant for.

Happy to answer questions about the setup, tooling, deployment pipeline, or what broke along the way.

App:
